title: edge quantization + fallback play brief for field ops (draft)
content:
Purpose:
A compact battle-brief + 6-slide speaker kit to help SEs and field ops quickly explain the tradeoffs when enabling quantized models for edge/private deployments and how Redwood’s runtime fallback policies keep latency and correctness within guardrails. Target audience: field SEs, technical account managers, platform integrators evaluating on-prem/edge pilots.

TL;DR (one-liner to lead with):
Enable aggressive quantization on constrained hardware to slash cost and memory while relying on Redwood’s smart fallback routing (model variants + dynamic dequantize-on-failure) to prevent customer-visible regressions.

Use cases to call out: 
- Mobile/edge assistants with tight memory (<=8GB GPU-equivalent)
- Appliance deployments (retail kiosks, in-vehicle assistants) that must run offline
- Regulated environments where on-prem inference cost must be predictable

Slide 1 — Opening frame (30s):
- Title: Edge tradeoffs: precision vs. throughput
- Hook: "Save up to 6x memory and 3x throughput — without letting errors reach users"
- Speaker note: start with quick customer anecdote (pilot with logistics partner reduced infra cost 4x but saw occasional hallucination spikes until fallback rules applied).

Slide 2 — The 3-tier quantization map (90s):
- Visual: Light/Medium/Aggr quantization tiers (fp16 -> int8 -> 4-bit/LLM.int4)
- Callouts: expected memory reduction, perf uplift, common failure modes (loss of specificity, token truncation, robustness to long context)
- Speaker note: emphasize predictability: medium tier often gives best tradeoff for long-context tasks.

Slide 3 — Failure modes & customer impact (60s):
- Bullet list: semantic drift, tokenization mismatch, higher repetition, rare truncation at long sequences
- Risk matrix: frequency x impact (rare-high, common-low etc.)
- Speaker note: be candid — quantify using pilot metrics when available.

Slide 4 — Redwood runtime mitigations (120s):
- Smart fallbacks: auto-route heavier model variant when quality checks fail (per-request or per-session)
- KV/prefix caching to keep hot prefixes on smaller variants while routing long-tail requests to full-precision variant
- Canary health checks & rolling thresholds (per-tenant eval hooks)
- Speaker note: map each mitigation to why it makes pilot-safe for customers. Mention autoscaling burst for private pools if latency SLOs spike.

Slide 5 — Customer objection cheat sheet (2–3 min):
- "What about hallucinations?" → We run continuous evals tied to prompt sets and fallback on quality regression triggers, with automatic rollbacks and canary holdifiers.
- "I need deterministic outputs." → Recommend medium quantization + dedicated pool; show token-level variance metrics from sample pilot.
- "We can’t send data off-prem." → All fallback routing stays within customer VPC; control plane only stores telemetry hashes (configurable).
- Speaker note: keep responses concise and cite internal pilot numbers when possible.

Slide 6 — Quick field playbook & triage checklist (1 page):
- Pre-pilot: pick baseline prompt set (50–200 high-value prompts), choose medium quantization first, reserve small burst capacity for heavy requests.
- During pilot: run hourly quality checks (accuracy + hallucination rate); enable auto-fallback threshold at X% degradation (suggested 5% for customer-facing chat).
- Post-pilot: collect failure examples, adjust quantization tier or add prompt-specific prefix cache.
- Rapid triage steps: 1) Check canary health dashboard 2) If degraded, enable immediate fallback to pinned model variant 3) Capture failure examples and open a ticket (ENG- tag)

Appendix — Quick technical bullets for deep-dive:
- Quantization knobs: per-channel vs per-tensor, symmetric vs asymmetric, outlier clipping thresholds, residual layer treatment.
- Runtime actions: dequantize-on-demand (costly but conservative), selective layer fp16 hybridization, fallthrough to cloud-hosted full-precision model for long-tail heavy queries.
- Observability signals to watch: per-token entropy, repetition score, answer length delta, user retention per-session.

Field ops scripts (short templates):
- Opening: "We recommend starting at the medium quant tier — it typically gives 2–3x memory reduction with minimal quality impact. If we see drift, our platform will transparently route affected requests to a higher-fidelity variant so your customers notice nothing."
- Escalation: "If we confirm a >5% regression on your key prompt set sustained over 2 hours, we switch to full-precision canary and engage an SRE runbook. We'll send failure examples and timeline within 30 minutes."

Known gaps & next steps (internal):
- Need updated quantization benchmark slides for Zephyrus hardware (ENG bench PR pending).
- Capture 3 anonymized customer failure examples for the sales cheat sheet.
- Add a short animation showing routing behavior for pitch deck v0.2.

Examples & data to attach during pitches: 
- Pilot metrics: memory reduction, 95th percentile latency change, hallucination-rate delta (before/after fallback).
- Short demo flow: show a request that trips quality check and gets smoothly routed to fallback with no client error.

Notes to SEs: keep technical depth variable — CIO/Procurement care about cost and determinism, integrators care about deployment complexity, SREs care about telemetry and rollback speed. Always have the 1-line TL;DR up front and an example metric in slide notes.

End.
